reuse.why: Extends the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend and threads the new field through every existing caller instead of adding a parallel holiday path.

duplication.why: The non-working-day rule is defined once (isNonWorkingDay), but the occurrence-window padding for holidays is restated ad hoc in three places with different factors (2x in getNextDate and getUpcomingDates, 3x in getDatesInRange).

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts, the module that already owns weekend adjustment; callers only forward their config.

scope.why: Only the type, the shared adjustment, its three callers, the rule parser and tests are touched.

maintainability.why: Clean generalisation of the weekend loop, though the function keeps a now-misleading weekend-only name and the per-caller margin heuristics are magic numbers a maintainer must keep consistent.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All callers (getNextDate, applyWeekendSkip, schedule-template getOccurrenceDay) go through getDateWithSkippedWeekend.

disguised_duplication.where: The holiday allowance for the occurrence window is written separately as `DAILY_CYCLE_LENGTH + 2 * holidays.length` (shared/schedules.ts getNextDate), `count * DAILY_CYCLE_LENGTH + 2 * holidays.length` (getUpcomingDates) and `HOLIDAY_SHIFT_DAYS * holidays.length` (getDatesInRange) instead of one shared margin.

one_place.where: shared/schedules.ts getDateWithSkippedWeekend/isNonWorkingDay decides weekend-or-holiday moves and daily skips; every caller passes config.holidays to it.
